message.content:
Here’s a practical step‑by‑step guide you can follow to pull up the full record for **“R v. Adams”** (or any other case).  
If you already know the docket number or the exact case ID used in your local court system, just let me know and I can fetch the details directly for you.

---

## 1️⃣ Identify the Court & Jurisdiction

| Question | Why it matters | Where to look |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| Which level of court handled the case? (e.g., state trial court, appellate court, federal district court) | Different courts have different public‑access portals. | Court’s official website; “About Us” or “Court Directory” pages |
| In which state or federal district was the case filed? | Determines the correct portal (PACER for federal, state court sites for state cases). | Court’s website; news articles; docket listings |

> **Tip:** If you only know the parties (“R v. Adams”), start by searching the name on the court’s *search* page. Many courts allow free searches by party name.

---

## 2️⃣ Find the Docket / Case ID

| How to locate | What to do |
|---------------|------------|
| **Online docket search** | Enter “Adams” (and optionally “R”) into the court’s docket search box. Filter by year or filing date if you have an approximate timeframe. |
| **Court clerk’s office** | Call or email the clerk’s office. Provide the parties’ names and any known dates; they can give you the docket number. |
| **Legal research services** | Services like Westlaw, LexisNexis, or Bloomberg Law often index cases by party name and provide the docket number automatically. |

> **Common docket formats**  
> • Federal: `Case No. 1:23‑CV‑01234`  
> • State: `Docket No. 2023‑12345`

---

## 3️⃣ Access the Full Record

| Platform | How to use it | Cost |
|----------|---------------|------|
| **PACER (U.S. federal)** | Go to [pacer.gov](https://www.pacer.gov/), log in (you’ll need a PACER account), then enter the docket number. | $0.10 per page (free for the first 10 pages per month) |
| **State court portal** | Most states have a “Public Access” or “Case Search” feature. After finding the docket, click “Documents” or “Full File.” | Usually free; some states charge a nominal fee |
| **CourtListener / Free Law Project** | Search by case name or docket; many documents are freely downloadable. | Free |
| **Legal research databases** | Westlaw/LexisNexis provide PDFs, transcripts, and metadata. | Subscription required |

> **Pro tip:** If the case is older than 7 years, many jurisdictions now offer the entire docket as a single PDF download—no per‑page fees.

---

## 4️⃣ Download & Organize

1. **Download all PDFs** (or use PACER’s “Bulk Download” if available).  
2. **Rename files** using a consistent scheme: `YYYYMMDD_Adams_R_v_Adams.pdf`.  
3. **Create a folder** labeled with the docket number for easy reference.  

---

## 5️⃣ Verify & Cross‑Reference

| Why verify? | How to do it |
|--------------|--------------|
| Ensure you have the right case (similar names can exist). | Check the case caption, judge’s name, and filing date against secondary sources (court opinions, news reports). |
| Confirm completeness of documents. | Compare the list of documents in the docket to what you’ve downloaded. |

---

## 6️⃣ Optional: Use the Assistant’s Function

If you can provide the **exact docket number** (e.g., `1:23‑CV‑01234`), I can retrieve the full case file for you:

```json
{
  "case_id": "1:23-CV-01234",
  "details": true
}
```

Just paste the docket number here, and I’ll call the function to fetch the data.

---

### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Identify court & jurisdiction  
- [ ] Locate docket number (via online search or clerk)  
- [ ] Access full record (PACER, state portal, or free service)  
- [ ] Download & rename files  
- [ ] Verify accuracy  

Let me know if you hit a snag at any step, or if you’d like me to fetch the case details once you have the docket number!
